title: Reliability and Redundancy
summary: Find single points of failure and compare resilient designs using safe hypothetical scenarios.
objectives: Identify a single point of failure in a simple diagram.
Compare reliability benefits with added resources and complexity.

vocab.def: The ability to continue or recover when a problem occurs.
Returning a system to an expected state after a disruption.
Planned work that helps a system continue operating.

sections.heading: Ask what happens if
sections.body: Designers test questions such as: What happens if this switch fails? What if a power path is interrupted? What if a cooling sensor gives a bad reading? These questions reveal dependencies.

sections.heading: More resilience has a cost
sections.body: A second switch, power path, or monitoring source may reduce risk. It may also require more equipment, energy, space, testing, and maintenance. Resilience is a reasoned choice, not a magic label.

sections.heading: Compare diagrams
sections.body: Circle the single point of failure in a one-path diagram, then add a conceptual alternate path. Explain what improved and what new design work remains.

practice.prompt: A design has two servers but one shared switch. What failure could affect both servers? Suggest a conceptual improvement and name one tradeoff.

quiz.question: What is a single point of failure?
options: One part whose failure can stop the larger system
quiz.answer: One part whose failure can stop the larger system

reflectionPrompt: Which failure question would reveal the most about a design you are building?
